source_refs.note: Exercise 11.1, Question 5: book page 290 (Q1-Q8). The book prints no answers for Unit 11; every answer here is ours.

blocks.explanation:
The components are given; we only combine them and state the domain.
As printed, \(x(t)\) contains \(r\), which is meant to be \(t\) (see the correction below): \(x(t) = t^2 + 1\).
Plan: vector form, then the domain as the intersection of the component domains.
steps:
Given: \(x(t) = t^2 + 1\) (printed \(r^2 + 1\)), \(y(t) = \sqrt{t}\).
To find: \(\mathbf{r}(t)\) and its domain.
Method: Step-2 and Step-3 of 11.1.3 (Step-1 is already done: the components are given). The domain is the set of \(t\) where every component is defined (11.2).

Combine into vector form
\[\mathbf{r}(t) = x(t)\,\hat{i} + y(t)\,\hat{j}\]
\[= (t^2 + 1)\,\hat{i} + \sqrt{t}\,\hat{j}\]
\[= \langle t^2 + 1, \sqrt{t}\rangle\]
Why: two components, so \(\mathbf{r}(t)\) is a 2D vector function; \(x\) goes with \(\hat{i}\), \(y\) with \(\hat{j}\).

Domain of each component
\(t^2 + 1\): defined for every real \(t\), domain \(\mathbb{R}\).
\(\sqrt{t}\): needs \(t \ge 0\), domain \([0, \infty)\).
Why: a polynomial has no restriction; the square root of a negative number is not real.

Intersection
\[\mathbb{R} \cap [0, \infty) = [0, \infty)\]
Why: \(t\) is allowed only if both components exist (Step-2 of 11.2.1).

Check with values
\[\mathbf{r}(0) = \hat{i},\quad \mathbf{r}(1) = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j}\]
\[\mathbf{r}(4) = 17\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}\]
\(\mathbf{r}(-1)\) does not exist, since \(\sqrt{-1}\) is not real \(\checkmark\).
Why: eliminating \(t\) (\(t = y^2\), \(y \ge 0\)) gives the path \(x = y^4 + 1\), which starts at \((1, 0)\).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints \(x(t) = r^2 + 1\). Here \(x\) is a function of \(t\), and \(r\) is the name of the vector function we are asked to build, so \(r^2\) makes no sense inside \(x(t)\). The intended component is \(x(t) = t^2 + 1\), which we use above.
